Comme s’il avait gagné un match de socce: As if he had just won a soccer game, Damas Porcena waves his arms in celebration, both fists raised in the air. The father of two children, aged two and four, is celebrating the Quebec Court of Appeal’s decision granting asylum seekers who hold a work permit the right to access subsidized daycares and early childhood centres (CPE). The ruling gives back their freedom to thousands of parents who have been deprived of this right since 2018.
« On se sent libéré ! Même si c’est notr: “We feel liberated! Even though she’s our daughter and we love her, we’re not free to move around, to work, to see people, to meet people,” says the 44-year-old man, originally from Haiti, who arrived six months ago with his wife and their two daughters.
Les juges de la Cour d’appel ont tranché: The Court of Appeal judges ruled in favour of the plaintiffs in a lawsuit brought against the Quebec government in 2018 by Bijou Cibuabua Kanyinda and the Quebec Human Rights Commission.
« Ma femme, elle a dit : “Je vais pouvoi: “My wife said, ‘I’m going to be able to go to school.’ We were so, so happy,” exclaims Porcena, whom La Converse met at the offices of Collectif Bienvenu. Energetic and jovial, he can barely contain his joy at the prospects finally opening up for him and his family.
« Normalement, quand on a un rendez-vous: “Normally, when we have an appointment, we have to take her with us in a stroller on the metro and the bus, even if it takes an hour or two. We always have to have her with us. We don’t have a choice.”
Dans sa décision, la juge de la Cour d’a: In her decision, Quebec Court of Appeal Justice Julie Dutil underlines the discriminatory nature of this exclusion.
« L’inclusion des personnes qui demanden: “Including people who claim asylum in section 3 of the RCR [Reduced Contribution Regulation] will moreover not have significant financial repercussions, since they do not have automatic access to the reduced contribution, but rather a possibility of obtaining it,” she writes.
« Je propose donc que l’article 3(3) du: “I therefore propose that section 3(3) of the RCR be read as making eligible for the reduced contribution the parent who resides in Quebec for the purposes of an asylum claim while holding a work permit.”

C’est en 2018 que le gouvernement provin: In 2018, Philippe Couillard’s provincial government changed the rules of the game and excluded the children of asylum seekers holding a work permit from subsidized daycare. They had had access to the same services from 2015 to 2018.
Bijou Cibuabua Kanyinda est la mère de t: Bijou Cibuabua Kanyinda is the mother of three children who were with her in Quebec when she decided to cross the border from the United States via Roxham Road. They were two, four and five years old when she filed her claim.
Alors qu’elle cherche des places pour se: When she looked for spots for her children in subsidized daycares, she was turned down because “access to these services [is] reserved for people whose refugee status is formally recognized by the federal authorities,” according to the legal documents.
Or, M<sup>me</sup> Kanyinda a son permis: But M<sup>me</sup> Kanyinda has a work permit, and the time between filing an asylum claim, the hearing and obtaining refugee status can take years. That is why she decided to turn to the courts.
D’autres organismes appuient sa demande,: Other organizations supported her case, including the Comité accès garderie and Amnesty International.
La Cour supérieure du Québec tranche en: The Quebec Superior Court ruled in favour of asylum seekers and their right to access subsidized daycare on May 25, 2022. Both parties appealed the judgment, for opposing reasons.
Dans le jugement du 7 février 2024, la j: In the February 7, 2024 judgment, Justice Julie Dutil found that denying asylum seekers access to subsidized daycares “reinforces and perpetuates the historical disadvantage experienced by women who wish to participate in the labour market. The distinction it creates by excluding people who claim asylum therefore constitutes discrimination.”
Et c’est justement cette discrimination: And it is precisely this gender-based discrimination that Ileana feels every day. The 30-year-old single mother arrived from Nicaragua alone and pregnant, but ran into many obstacles. “I’ve seen very difficult cases where mothers break down psychologically, like I did,” she says. “It affects us a lot, because we get discouraged, and we tell ourselves: ‘I won’t be able to connect with anyone.’ We stay isolated at home, we can’t even volunteer. We can’t because we don’t have access to daycare.”
Si le procureur général du Québec, qui r: If the Attorney General of Quebec, who represents the province, decides to challenge the Court of Appeal’s judgment, the case will head to the Supreme Court of Canada.
Il faut cependant que la plus haute inst: However, the country’s highest court would have to agree to hear it. At the Ministry of Family, it is too early to announce next steps. “We are still reviewing [the decision],” the ministry’s press attaché explains in an email. “It is too early to comment on the effects of the Court’s decision on the network of educational childcare services.”
Selon les données les plus récentes du m: According to the Ministry of Family’s most recent data, <l1>32,113 children are waiting for a spot in subsidized daycare</l1>.
Qualifié d’historique en raison de sa re: Described as historic because it recognizes discrimination against women in a subgroup, namely asylum seekers, the Court of Appeal’s judgment has delighted one of the lawyers on the case, M<sup>e</sup> Guillaume Grenier, who calls the decision “thorough.”
« Nous trouvons que le jugement est extr: “We find the judgment extremely solid, and we hope the government will take note of it and won’t appeal the judgment,” says the lawyer, who has been handling the case with his colleague M<sup>e</sup> Sibel Ataogul since 2019.
Sur une note plus personnelle, M<sup>e</: On a more personal note, M<sup>e</sup> Grenier realizes the significance of his work, which he sees as a culmination. “It’s extremely moving. I heard the testimonies [of the women asylum seekers], and even now, it moves me. You can’t remain indifferent to that. In the end, it’s what drives our work.”
Si la garderie offre un bon programme éd: While daycare offers children a good educational program, <l1>its benefits for their development are also many</l1>. These places where toddlers spend their days allow children to socialize, but also to acquire skills that will be useful to them in kindergarten. And this integration is all the more important for children who don’t speak French at home, notes Mélissa Claisse of Collectif Bienvenu.
« Avoir un très bon accès aux conditions: “Having really good access to the conditions for learning the language is huge for these children. On top of that, being in an early childhood education setting gives them access to screening for developmental problems,” she says, having witnessed situations where children were followed up on much later for a learning difficulty.
« Ils n’y auraient pas accès s’ils resta: “They wouldn’t have access to that if they stayed at home. And for children who have these problems, early intervention makes an immense difference.”
Et on peut ajouter que la socialisation: And socializing isn’t only for the little ones – parents benefit too. “With access to daycare, now that I’m being told it’s possible [to bring my daughter], you can’t imagine how I feel,” exclaims Ileana, her one-year-old daughter in her arms. The little girl has a fever and doesn’t want to leave her mother’s arms.
« C’est comme si beaucoup de portes s’ou: “It’s as if many doors were opening! And the possibilities are endless for me. Whether it’s to integrate, to support organizations, to volunteer, to work, to study, you understand?”
Le premier souhait de cette mère monopar: This single mother’s first wish? To take French classes and integrate into Quebec society as quickly as possible. “I was losing hope… To learn the language and have richer conversations with other people. Integration is also about being autonomous,” she says thoughtfully, gently rocking her little girl.
Le visage d’Ileana s’illumine à l’évocat: Ileana’s face lights up at the mention of this possibility. She is constantly struggling to make herself understood in a system where she speaks neither French nor English, especially when it comes to seeking care for her daughter. Without daycare, it’s very hard.
Les intervenants du Collectif Bienvenu p: Collectif Bienvenu’s staff can attest to the effects of this step forward, both in accessing the labour market and in taking French classes. And they believe women are the ones who will benefit.
« Je connais au moins une centaine de pe: “I know at least a hundred people who have training as care workers and who could be working right now,” says Maryse Poisson, executive director of the organization, which helps refugees and asylum seekers.
Quand on leur demande ce qu’ils diraient: Asked what they would say to political decision-makers if they were tempted to appeal the Quebec Court of Appeal’s judgment and take the case all the way to the Supreme Court, Porcena and Ileana are unanimous: taking away their access to subsidized daycare would be like slamming doors in their faces and taking opportunities away from them.
« Quand on arrive ici [comme demandeurs: “When we arrive here [as asylum seekers], integration is difficult. We really need it,” says Porcena, who then apologizes for being in a hurry to leave.
« Maintenant, je dois retourner chez moi: “Now I have to go home because my wife has an appointment; I have to take over. It disrupts [my schedule]; if my daughter were in daycare, my wife would be free to go out without me having to come back home.”
Mélissa Claisse, du Collectif Bienvenu,: Mélissa Claisse of Collectif Bienvenu hopes Quebec will recognize the immense difference that access to subsidized daycare could make. “Recently, François Legault specifically mentioned the burden that asylum seekers represent for the social assistance program. This is the perfect example of a way to make an enormous difference in that area. Access to employment means getting off social assistance. And families don’t want to depend on social assistance.”
Et qui plus est, les demandeurs d’asile: What’s more, asylum seekers want to contribute to society – that is Ileana’s conviction.
« Si on retire cette opportunité, beauco: “If this opportunity is taken away, many, many, many asylum seekers will leave, because they’ll lose their illusions. They’re tired of fighting, of trying to integrate without being able to. It makes them feel... how do I put it? Rejected. I know several people here who think it would be better to turn back and stop fighting.”
